label: Bible Study
prompt: Let the words of my mouth, and the _____ of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.
verse: Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.
note: The closing prayer of the sky-and-Scripture psalm — many a sermon still begins with it.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And thou shalt be secure, because there is _____; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety.
verse: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt take thy rest in safety.
note: Zophar promises Job security 'because there is hope' — rest in safety, even after the worst.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And a certain man lame from his mother's womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called _____, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple;
verse: And a certain man lame from his mother's womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple;
note: A lame man begged daily at the temple gate called Beautiful — until Peter offered something better than alms.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force _____.
verse: And Moses was an hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
note: At 120, Moses still had sharp eyes and full strength — he didn't fade out, he was simply called home.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Wherefore the LORD God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly _____.
verse: Wherefore the LORD God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.
note: Spoken against Eli's house — and slipped to Eric Liddell in a note before his 1924 Olympic 400m final, which he won.
